# KBD Constraints — Charcoal Agent

Generated by `/kbd-init` on 2026-09-23. The project has no `AGENTS.md` "Never Do"
section, so the blocking rules below are the generic KBD defaults adapted to this
stack (Vite/React/TypeScript + Tauri shell) plus rules derived from `CLAUDE.md`.

Commands use `npm` (Dockerfile builds with `npm ci`; `package-lock.json` is the
authoritative lockfile). No mandatory command wrapper or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` policy
is defined for this project.

Path ownership: `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.opencode/`, `.kimi-code/` and `openspec/`
are repository-owned tool configuration (OpenSpec skills/commands), not disposable
state — do not delete or regenerate them as part of a change. Reference workspace
folders (see `project.json` → `workspace.folders`) are read-only.

---

## Blocking Constraints (prevent archiving until resolved)

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Vite production build must pass'
    command: 'npm run build'

  - id: tests-pass
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Vitest suite must pass (skills-sync integration test self-skips without a UAR)'
    command: 'npm test'

  - id: no-console-log-in-commits
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No console.log in committed TypeScript (console.error/warn for real error paths is allowed)'
    check: "grep -rn 'console\\.log' src/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'"

  - id: no-any-type
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No new `: any` in TypeScript source (1 pre-existing occurrence at init; do not add more)'
    check: "grep -rn ': any' src/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'"

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No hardcoded API keys/tokens; UAR auth comes only from VITE_UAR_API_KEY'
    check: "grep -rn 'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]\\{8,\\}\\|Bearer [A-Za-z0-9]\\{16,\\}' src/"

  - id: no-env-files-committed
    severity: blocking
    description: '.env and .env.*.local must never be committed (only .env.example)'
    check: "git ls-files | grep -E '^\\.env($|\\.)' | grep -v '^\\.env\\.example$'"

  - id: reference-folders-read-only
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No writes to reference workspace folders (UAR, artifact-refiner, openfang)'
    note: 'Changes to the UAR contract are made in that repo separately; this project only consumes it'

  - id: pglite-migrations-append-only
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Existing entries in MIGRATIONS (src/lib/db/pglite.ts) must not be edited; add a new version instead'
    note: 'Review git diff of src/lib/db/pglite.ts'

  - id: pglite-not-prebundled
    severity: blocking
    description: '@electric-sql/pglite must remain in vite.config.ts optimizeDeps.exclude'
    check: "grep -q 'exclude: \\[\"@electric-sql/pglite\"\\]' vite.config.ts || echo MISSING"
```

---

## Warning Constraints (acknowledge before archiving)

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: no-lint-warnings
    severity: warning
    description: 'ESLint clean'
    command: 'npm run lint'

  - id: agui-contract-parity
    severity: warning
    description: 'New/changed AG-UI event handling in use-message-stream.ts matches UAR src/uar/api/sse.rs'
    note: 'Cross-check against the reference folder; flows are type → store action → stream case → render component'

  - id: assistant-ui-metadata
    severity: warning
    description: 'Every ThreadMessageLike produced in use-chat-runtime.ts carries metadata (and user messages attachments: [])'
    note: 'Manual review — missing fields crash @assistant-ui/react internals'

  - id: shadcn-components
    severity: warning
    description: 'UI uses shadcn/ui components from src/components/ui rather than raw HTML controls'

  - id: tests-for-new-features
    severity: warning
    description: 'Tests exist for new hooks, stores and utilities added in this change'

  - id: no-stub-comments
    severity: warning
    description: 'No TODO/FIXME/STUB/HACK comments in committed code'
    check: "grep -rn 'TODO\\|FIXME\\|STUB\\|HACK' src/"

  - id: accessibility-basics
    severity: warning
    description: 'New UI components have aria-label or semantic HTML'
    note: 'Manual review required'
```

---

## Workflow Triggers

```yaml
workflow_triggers:
  - event: on_iteration_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm run build'

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm test && npm run lint'

  - event: on_refinement_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: "git add -A && git commit -m 'kbd: refine <change-id>'"
```

===== plan.md =====
# Plan: uar-integration

Planned 2026-09-30 from `assessment.md` and the operator decisions D1–D4, with Q7 and Q8 at their defaults.

**Operator input since assess.** The Cloudflare record is added. `runtime.know-me.tools` resolves to `23.239.29.33` (checked with `dig`).

**Backend.** OpenSpec, in this repo, for all six changes. Changes 1 and 4 land in other repos (`Prometheus-AGS/universal-agent-runtime` and `Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster`). Their OpenSpec folders here track the task list and record the external PR as evidence.

## Resolved defaults used by this plan

| Question | Value |
|---|---|
| Q1 hostname | `runtime.know-me.tools` (the DNS record exists) |
| Q2 DNS and listener | The operator did DNS. We open the `know-me-cluster` PR and the operator merges it |
| Q3 auth | `UAR_SECURITY__JWT_REQUIRED=true` in the cluster. HS256 secret from a GitHub secret; `settings_admin_key` set. Local compose stays `false` |
| Q5 UI | Only UAR is deployed. The local UI reaches the cluster UAR only through an explicit `VITE_UAR_BASE_URL` |
| Q6 Token Plan terms | The operator confirms before change 5 goes live. Recorded as a precondition, not a task |
| Q7 image bumps | Renovate PRs bump the pinned digest in `k8s/` |
| Q8 ACR and AKS | `deploy.yml`'s ACR push and AKS jobs stay untouched; GHCR is added |

## Ordered changes

### 1. `uar-ghcr-multiarch-publish`

- **Repo:** UAR, as a PR to `Prometheus-AGS/universal-agent-runtime`.
- **Agent:** km-devops-engineer.
- **Depends on:** nothing.

**What.** Add jobs that build the existing `Dockerfile` natively:
- on `ubuntu-24.04` for linux/amd64
- on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` for linux/arm64

Each architecture pushes by digest to `ghcr.io/prometheus-ags/universal-agent-runtime`. A merge job creates one manifest list, tagged with the commit SHA and `main`, plus `vX.Y.Z` on version tags. Auth is `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `packages: write`. The jobs reuse the existing `SUBMODULES_TOKEN` and `github_token` build secret, and each gets a free-disk step and a per-architecture GHA cache scope.

**Done when:**
- a workflow run on `main` is green
- `docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/prometheus-ags/universal-agent-runtime:main` lists both platforms
- an anonymous `docker pull` works, once the operator has made the package public (D3)

**Risks:**
- The build takes 45–75 minutes per architecture.
- The arm64 toolchain (TinyGo, wasmtime and Go on arm64) has never been built. If it fails, stop and report; do not fall back to QEMU without asking.

### 2. `local-compose-published-uar`

- **Repo:** this one.
- **Agent:** km-devops-engineer.
- **Depends on:** 1 (a pullable `:main` image).

**Tasks:**
1. Check against the image from change 1:
   - the env-var spelling for nested config (`UAR_LLM__EMBEDDING__BASE_URL` and friends)
   - the model prefix for an OpenAI-compatible custom base (`openai/qwen3.8-max` vs `qwen3.8-max` with `LLM_PROTOCOL`)
   - whether knowledge bases inherit `llm.embedding` or need their own override
2. `docker-compose.yaml`:
   - `uar` uses `image: ghcr.io/prometheus-ags/universal-agent-runtime:main`, with the build block removed (D1)
   - the healthcheck is `curl -fsS http://localhost:6565/readyz`
   - the chat model, embedding backend, model, base URL, key and `dimensions=1024` come from `.env`
   - `UAR_PERSISTENCE__VECTOR_DIMENSION=1024`
   - `UAR_SECURITY__SETTINGS_ADMIN_KEY` comes from `.env`
3. Git-ignored `.env`: add the `UAR_*`/`LLM_*` names compose reads, set from the existing values. `.env.example`: names and placeholders only, with Qwen defaults and 1024 dimensions documented.
4. Document that the old `uar_data` volume must be removed, because its vectors are 384-dimensional.

**Done when (the live smoke carried from complete-rebranding):**
- `docker compose up` shows `uar` healthy and `knowme-web` serving on :8080
- through the nginx proxy, `/api/chat/completion` streams a `qwen3.8-max` reply
- a knowledge-base or memory embedding call succeeds with 1024-dimension vectors
- the command output and a screenshot of the chat are recorded

### 3. `k8s-uar-manifests`

- **Repo:** this one (`k8s/`).
- **Agent:** km-devops-engineer; km-security-officer reviews.
- **Depends on:** 1 (the image digest).

**What.** Kustomize base with:
- namespace `knowme-runtime`
- a Deployment: one replica, `strategy: Recreate` (RWO volume), image pinned by digest, `envFrom` from ConfigMap `uar-config` and Secret `uar-secrets`, liveness `/healthz` and readiness `/readyz` on 6565, resource requests and limits, non-root securityContext
- Service :6565
- a PVC, 10Gi, `linode-block-storage-retain`
- an HTTPRoute for `runtime.know-me.tools`, with parentRef `argocd/argocd-gateway` and sectionName `knowme-runtime-https`, carrying a 300s request timeout for SSE
- an HTTP→HTTPS redirect HTTPRoute on `knowme-runtime-http`
- ConfigMap `uar-config` with the non-secret settings: model ids, base URLs, dimensions, `JWT_REQUIRED=true`
- `k8s/bootstrap/`: a namespace-scoped ServiceAccount, Role and RoleBinding for the deployer, plus a script the operator runs once with the admin context to mint a namespace-limited kubeconfig

There is no Secret manifest; change 5 creates the Secret from GitHub secrets. `renovate.json` covers the digest in `k8s/`.

**Done when:**
- `kubectl kustomize k8s` renders
- `kubectl --context know-me apply -k k8s --dry-run=server` succeeds
- no secret value appears in any tracked file (grep check)

### 4. `gateway-listener-runtime`

- **Repo:** a PR to `Prometheus-AGS/know-me-cluster`, which the operator merges.
- **Agent:** km-devops-engineer.
- **Depends on:** nothing. It can run in parallel with 1–3.

**What.** In `namespaces/argocd-config/manifests.yaml`, add to `argocd-gateway`:
- listener `knowme-runtime-https`: hostname `runtime.know-me.tools`, port 443, TLS secret `wildcard-know-me-tools-tls`, `allowedRoutes` All
- listener `knowme-runtime-http`: the same hostname, port 80

These mirror the existing `flint-rt-*` pair. No new Certificate is needed: the wildcard covers the host.

**Done when:**
- the PR is merged
- Argo `argocd-config` shows Synced and Healthy
- `kubectl --context know-me -n argocd get gateway argocd-gateway -o json` shows both listeners with Programmed=True

### 5. `github-deploy-uar-workflow`

- **Repo:** this one (`.github/workflows/deploy-uar.yml`).
- **Agent:** km-devops-engineer; km-security-officer reviews.
- **Depends on:** 3 and 4; Q6 confirmed.

**Triggers.** `workflow_dispatch`, plus pushes to `main` that touch `k8s/**`. The trigger includes Renovate's digest PRs once merged.

**Steps:**
1. Write a kubeconfig from secret `KNOWME_RUNTIME_KUBECONFIG` (namespace-scoped, from change 3).
2. Create or update Secret `uar-secrets` idempotently (`kubectl create secret generic … --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`) from these GitHub secrets:
   - `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY`
   - `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`
   - `UAR_JWT_SECRET`
   - `UAR_SETTINGS_ADMIN_KEY`
3. `kubectl apply -k k8s`.
4. `rollout status`.
5. Smoke-test the public URL.

The operator adds the GitHub secrets (`gh secret set`); agents never handle the values.

**Done when a workflow run is green and the run's smoke test shows:**
- `https://runtime.know-me.tools/readyz` → 200, with a valid certificate
- `/api/agents` without a token → 401
- with an HS256 JWT minted in the job from `UAR_JWT_SECRET` → 200
- one chat completion returns `qwen3.8-max` output

### 6. `about-endpoint-truth`

- **Repo:** this one.
- **Agent:** km-frontend-engineer.
- **Depends on:** 2.

**What.** Landing follow-up S5: when `VITE_UAR_BASE_URL` is unset, the About page's endpoint row shows the actual same-origin proxy target, not a guessed default. It follows the `visual-first-ui-delivery` capture at 320 and 1440 px in both themes.

**Done when:**
- the unit test for the endpoint label passes
- screenshots have been viewed and are listed
- the existing goldens pass, or are updated with operator sign-off

## Ordering rationale

- **Change 1 blocks 2, 3 and 5,** because each consumes the published image.
- **Change 4 has no dependency.** It starts at once because it waits on an operator merge.
- **Change 5 runs last.** It is the only step that makes the runtime public, so it waits for auth (the 3 ConfigMap), the listener (4) and Q6.
- **Change 6 is small UI work.** It follows the local stack (2) so the label can be checked against a real endpoint.

## Operator actions (not agent tasks)

1. Make the GHCR package public in the UI after change 1's first run (D3).
2. Merge the `know-me-cluster` PR (change 4).
3. Run `k8s/bootstrap` once with the admin context. Then `gh secret set` for:
   - `KNOWME_RUNTIME_KUBECONFIG`
   - `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY`
   - `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`
   - `UAR_JWT_SECRET`
   - `UAR_SETTINGS_ADMIN_KEY`
4. Confirm the Token Plan terms (Q6). Rotate the DashScope key after setup.
5. Install the Renovate GitHub App on this repo if the org doesn't have it.

## The uncomfortable part

- **A long, untested build is the critical path.**
  - Changes 2, 3 and 5 all wait on change 1.
  - Change 1 is a 45–75 minute build per architecture, and the arm64 toolchain has never been built.
  - A failure there stalls the phase.
  - The fallback, amd64 only with emulation on the Mac, needs an operator decision.
- **The client can't authenticate to the public runtime.**
  - `VITE_UAR_API_KEY` is compiled into the SPA bundle.
  - A JWT placed there is readable by anyone who loads the page.
  - This phase deploys only UAR, so that is acceptable for local builds only.
  - Any public UI deploy needs a real token flow first (for example via the cluster's Kratos at `auth.know-me.tools`). That is out of scope here.

# Goals

Operator request, 2026-09-30. Credentials are redacted here: they live only in git-ignored `.env` files.

1. **Local UAR in Docker.** Build a Docker image from `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/universal-agent-runtime` and run it through this repo's `docker-compose.yaml` for local testing, alongside the KnowMe UI.
2. **Kubernetes deployment in `k8s/`.** Put the manifests for a UAR deployment on the `know-me` kubectl context in the `k8s/` subdirectory. Configuration comes from Kubernetes secrets, never literals.
3. **Public DNS and TLS.** Serve the instance at an appropriate `<name>.know-me.tools` host. Share the cluster's **existing Envoy Gateway** rather than installing another. For TLS, use cert-manager with Let's Encrypt, or reuse an existing wildcard certificate for `*.know-me.tools` if one exists.
4. **GitHub Actions deploy.** A workflow that builds the image and deploys it to the `know-me` context using the `k8s/` config, with credentials and settings supplied as GitHub secrets.
5. **Default chat model configured automatically.** UAR's embedded liter-llm settings use the operator-specified Qwen "3.8 max" model through the Alibaba Token Plan. The key and URL are in `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/know-me/know-me-decision/.env`. The exact model id must be confirmed from Alibaba documentation, not guessed. It becomes the default model, so the deployed UAR has a working model.
6. **Default embedding model.** A Qwen embedding model through DashScope's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`), using a DashScope API key the operator supplied in session.
   - The model id comes from web research.
   - The key is written to `know-me-decision/.env`, never to a tracked file.
7. **Local `.env`.** A git-ignored `.env` in this repo holds every setting needed to run the stack locally.
8. **Carried from complete-rebranding:**
   - the deferred live UAR smoke test against the real runtime
   - About-page endpoint truth (landing S5)

## Constraints
- No secret in any tracked file, commit, PR, log or `goals.md`. Local development uses `.env`; the cluster uses Kubernetes secrets populated from GitHub secrets.
- The operator pasted the DashScope key in chat. It has therefore been exposed in the session transcript; rotating it after setup is recommended.
- Reuse the existing cluster infrastructure (Envoy Gateway, cert-manager) and install nothing that already exists.
